description:
Read only the profiler report from the previous task and produce an executable NAS search space plan in JSON.
Behavior requirements: - Be conservative and pragmatic. - Prefer simple, well-established model families. - Include only model families clearly supported by profiler evidence. - Use small, bounded, realistic hyperparameter ranges. - Prefer categorical choices and small discrete ranges over wide continuous spaces. - Express uncertainty when profiler evidence is incomplete.
Strict constraints: - Do not inspect raw datasets. - Do not call dataset inspection tools. - Do not train models. - Do not run Optuna. - Do not evaluate model performance. - Do not select a final model.
Output must be strict JSON only (no markdown, no code fences, no prose before/after JSON).
\n\nInput: use only the profiler report generated by the previous task.

key_constraints: High feature-to-sample ratio (2,500 features vs 2,660 samples)
Overfitting risk due to small sample size

selected_model_families.rationale: The profiler identifies the data as a digitized 1D signal (ECG). CNN1D is the standard architecture for capturing local temporal patterns in signals while managing feature dimensionality through pooling or strides.
The data is provided in a flattened CSV format. A simple MLP serves as a necessary baseline, though it is high-risk for overfitting given the 1:1 ratio of features to samples.

uncertainty_notes: Sampling frequency is unknown; kernel sizes are estimated without physical time context.
Data normalization status is unknown; models may require an internal Batch Normalization layer.
Lack of Patient ID means subject-level splitting is impossible, potentially inflating performance metrics.
handoff_notes: Reshape input from (2500,) to (2500, 1) for cnn1d family.
Strong regularization (Dropout > 0.3) is recommended due to the high feature-to-sample ratio.
Use Stratified K-Fold validation to maintain the balance between 'Normal' and 'Sleep Apnea' classes.
